lines.text: DeepSeek-V2 has two hundred and thirty-six billion parameters.
And on any given token, only twenty-one billion of them are used.
That is a mixture of experts. A router reads the token and picks eight experts out of a hundred and sixty.
A hundred and fifty-two never run at all. And two shared experts always do.
So the compute you pay for is the compute of a twenty-one-billion model.
But the memory you need is still two hundred and thirty-six billion parameters. All of them are stored.
Sparse compute, dense storage. That is the deal.
It is a good one for throughput, and a bad one for your disk bill.
And there is a cost that does not show up in either number. The router has to be right.
Pick the wrong expert and the token goes through a network that was never trained for it.
So the router has to be balanced. Send too much to one expert and the rest go stale.
Most of these models also run a couple of dense experts on every token, so no token is completely unrouted.
Two hundred and thirty-six billion parameters. Twenty-one billion working. Both numbers are true.
